docs.title: λORM
docs.text:
λORM (LambdaORM) is a TypeScript ORM that runs distributed queries across different database engines: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB and SQLite.

Queries are written as lambda expressions over a domain model that is independent of the infrastructure. A single query can read or write entities stored in different databases — for example, some in MySQL, others in PostgreSQL and others in MongoDB — and λORM splits it into one sentence per source and joins the results.

The same domain can have several stages (infrastructure scenarios). In one stage the data may be spread across SQL Server, MongoDB and Oracle; in another, everything may live in a single PostgreSQL database. This makes it possible to implement patterns such as CQRS through configuration, without changing the code.

See the features for a complete list.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
Way Package When to use it Node.js library @lambdaorm/lib Run queries from a Node.js / TypeScript application. See Usage. Command line @lambdaorm/cli (command lambdaorm) Create a project, synchronize the databases, import and export data, and run queries from a terminal or CI. See CLI. Data Gateway Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway Expose λORM schemas over the network: a REST API, MCP for AI agents, a WebSocket API and a web UI. See Data Gateway. Node.js client @lambdaorm/client Run the same queries from Node.js against a Data Gateway. See Clients. 
npm install @lambdaorm/lib      # the library
npm install -g @lambdaorm/cli   # the lambdaorm command

Note

The unscoped packages lambdaorm, lambdaorm-cli and lambdaorm-client-node are no longer maintained: use the @lambdaorm/* packages.

docs.title: Query language
docs.text:
The following query returns the highest price of each product category, considering only the products that match the filter and the categories whose highest price is above 50:

import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/lib'
import { Products } from './northwind/domain/model'

const query = (country: string) => Products
  .filter(p => (p.price > 5 && p.supplier.country == country) || (p.inStock < 3))
  .having(p => max(p.price) > 50)
  .map(p => ({ category: p.category.name, largestPrice: max(p.price) }))
  .sort(p => desc(p.largestPrice))

await orm.init('./lambdaORM.yaml')
// run the query, passing the value of the country parameter
const result = await orm.execute(query, { country: 'ARG' })
await orm.end()

In this query:

  • filter keeps the products whose price is greater than 5 and whose supplier is in the given country, as well as those with fewer than 3 units in stock.
  • map returns the category name and the highest price. Grouping is implicit: the products are grouped by category because max is an aggregate function.
  • having keeps only the categories whose highest price is greater than 50.
  • sort orders the result by the highest price, in descending order.
  • supplier and category are relations: the joins are implicit.

See also: query language | select | join | grouping | include | insert | bulk insert | update | delete | metadata | repository | usage

docs.title: Include
docs.text:
include returns an entity together with its relations in the same query, even when they are stored in different databases. In this example the query is written as a string, an alternative to the lambda expression:

import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/lib'

(async () => {
  try {
    await orm.init('./config/northwind.yaml')
    const query = `Orders
      .filter(p => p.id === id)
      .include(p => [
        p.customer.map(p => p.name),
        p.details
          .include(p => p.product
            .include(p => p.category.map(p => p.name))
            .map(p => p.name))
          .map(p => [p.quantity, p.unitPrice])
      ])`
    const result = await orm.execute(query, { id: 102 }, { stage: 'PostgreSQL' })
    console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2))
  } catch (error: any) {
    console.error(error.message)
  } finally {
    await orm.end()
  }
})()

Result:

[
  {
    "id": 102,
    "customerId": "SPLIR",
    "employeeId": 7,
    "orderDate": "1996-11-07T23:00:00.000Z",
    "requiredDate": "1996-12-05T23:00:00.000Z",
    "shippedDate": "1996-11-14T23:00:00.000Z",
    "shipViaId": 1,
    "freight": 8.63,
    "name": "Split Rail Beer & Ale",
    "address": "P.O. Box 555",
    "city": "Lander",
    "region": "WY",
    "postalCode": "82520",
    "country": "USA",
    "customer": {
      "name": "Split Rail Beer & Ale"
    },

]

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
The schema defines entities, enumerations, indexes, unique keys, default values, constraints, mappings, sources, stages, listeners and more. It is written in YAML or JSON. Conditions and actions use the same expression language as queries.

See also: schema | definition | use | expressions | environment variables | composite | listeners | multiple stages | multiple sources | engines

docs.title: Synchronization
docs.text: λORM keeps the databases and the schema in step, in both directions: synchronization | push | pull | fetch | introspect | incorporate

docs.title: Transactions and scripts
docs.text:
• Transactions: orm.transaction runs several queries in one transaction, also across sources and stages.
  • Scripts: a whole use case (variables, conditions, loops and several queries) in one transaction and in a single call — from Node.js, the CLI or the Data Gateway.

docs.title: Labs
docs.text: Complete examples are available in the λORM labs.

docs.title: Related projects
docs.text:
• λORM CLI: command line interface for λORM.
  • Data Gateway: λORM schemas over REST, MCP and WebSocket, with a web UI.
  • λORM client: Node.js client for the Data Gateway.
  • 3xpr: extensible expression engine that evaluates mathematical and logical expressions; λORM queries and scripts are built on it.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: An overview of what λORM offers, with links to the pages that describe each feature.

docs.title: Database engines
docs.text:
• MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB and SQLite (SQLjs).
  • A single query can involve several databases, even of different engines.
  • Engines: the differences between engines (types, empty strings, upsert, …).

docs.title: Query language
docs.text:
• Query language based on JavaScript lambda expressions.
  • Queries can be written as JavaScript/TypeScript code or as a string.
  • Select, insert, bulk insert, update and delete clauses.
  • Implicit joins and grouping.
  • Eager loading of relations with include, also across databases.
  • Operators and functions.
  • Query metadata: the parameters, model, constraints and execution plan of a query.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
• Repositories and custom repositories.
  • Transactions and distributed transactions, across sources and stages.
  • Scripts: a whole use case (variables, conditions, loops and several queries) in one transaction, also over the Data Gateway.
  • Usage examples: a single source, several sources, CQRS and the Node.js client.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
• Schema configuration that decouples the domain model from the infrastructure.
  • Configuration in JSON or YAML.
  • Mappings between the domain and the infrastructure.
  • Entity inheritance (extends).
  • Environment variables.
  • Indexes, unique keys and constraints.
  • Conditions and actions based on the 3xpr expression engine (expressions).
  • Stages: several infrastructure scenarios for the same domain.
  • Synchronization between the schema and the databases: push, pull, fetch, introspect and incorporate.
  • Listeners and subscribers: awaited, and run in the transaction of the sentence that triggers them.

docs.title: Tools and clients
docs.text:
• TypeScript and JavaScript support.
  • CLI (npm i -g @lambdaorm/cli, command lambdaorm).
  • Data Gateway (Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway):
    • a REST API, MCP for AI agents and a WebSocket API, with several schemas per instance;
    • credentials with permissions, audit of writes, metrics and health checks;
    • a web UI: explorer, entity forms, saved queries and diagrams of the domain.
  • Clients:
    • Node.js client (@lambdaorm/client, REST or WebSocket);
    • other languages: generate a client from the Data Gateway's OpenAPI 3 document.

docs.title: λORM CLI
docs.text: The λORM CLI (@lambdaorm/cli) is a command line application to use λORM: it creates projects, synchronizes the databases with the schema, imports and exports data, and runs queries and scripts. Its commands run locally with a workspace (-w), and most of them can also run on a Data Gateway (-u <url>).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the package globally; it adds the lambdaorm command:

npm i -g @lambdaorm/cli
lambdaorm --version

It requires Node.js 20 or later. The Docker image of the Data Gateway (flaviorita/data-gateway) already includes the CLI.

Note

The unscoped lambdaorm-cli package is the old one and is no longer maintained.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Description version Prints the CLI version and the @lambdaorm/lib version the project uses. init Generates the structure of a λORM project. build Generates the model and the repositories for the language. schema Returns information about the schema. push Synchronizes the databases with the model (-o writes the scripts instead). pull Updates the schema with the structure of the databases of a stage. fetch Shows the differences between the databases and the model; exits with code 1 when there are any. introspect Reads and analyzes a data file and updates the schema. incorporate Updates the schema from a data file, pushes the changes to the databases and imports the data. drop Removes all the database objects, but not the database itself. import Imports data from a file into the databases. export Exports data from the databases. execute Executes a query. script Runs a script: several queries in one transaction. plan Returns the execution plan of a query. metadata Returns the metadata of a query. parameters Returns the parameters of a query. model Returns the model of the result of a query. constraints Returns the constraints of a query.

lambdaorm <command> -h lists the options of a command; lambdaorm -h lists the commands.

The sync command no longer exists: it was replaced by push.

docs.title: Common options
docs.text:
Option Short Description workspace -w Path of the project (the folder with lambdaORM.yaml). Default: the current directory. stage -s Name of the stage. Default: the first stage of the schema. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables (for example the connection strings). output -o Output format of the result: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there instead of locally.

Each command page lists the options that command accepts.

docs.title: Exit code and Data Gateway
docs.text:
Every command exits with code 1 when it fails (from @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3).

Commands run on a Data Gateway with -u and the URL of the schema, for example http://gateway:8080/iot/v1. When the SERVICE_TOKEN environment variable is set, it is sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> (for a gateway with bearer authentication). See also Clients.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text:
• 0e683c6: Scripts: several queries in one transaction.

  • client: orm.executeScript(script, data, options) calls the service's POST /script (the service must run with SCRIPT_ENABLED=true).

  • cli: new lambdaorm script command, with the script inline (-x) or in a file (-f), its variables in -d; local with the workspace or on a service with -u.

  • d16b60a: stage.push().sentencesBySource(): the DDL grouped per source (one script per database). cli: lambdaorm push -o <dir> writes one script per source that changes, <stage>.<source>.sql (deterministic names, to rename into a versioned migration); -o without a folder prints the DDL grouped by source — L19.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• 2ee8930: Upgrade the data7expressions dependencies to their latest major: 3xpr from 1.x to ^5.1.1, h3lp and typ3s to ^5.0.0 (and json-light to ^5.0.0 in the CLI). No API changes were needed. Behaviour inherited from 3xpr:

  • <= now has the same precedence as the other comparison operators (a <= b == true used to evaluate as a <= (b == true)).

  • 3xpr 5.1.0 evaluates async expressions statement by statement (listeners, orm.execute inside expressions), never runs an async function while building an expression, and adds throw, try/catch, return, break and continue; 3xpr 5.1.1 parses the empty string literal "" (it used to swallow the rest of the expression).

  • ee1e7ac: Packaging:

  • The published exports pointed to ./build/lib/index.js, a path the package doesn't have: require('@lambdaorm/lib') (and base, client) failed for everyone installing from npm. dist now rewrites exports (and bin) like main — L7.

  • cli: declares bin: lambdaorm, so npm i -g @lambdaorm/cli installs the lambdaorm command — L29.

  • Every package's dist is smoke-tested before it can be released: required by its name (so exports applies) and, for the CLI, lambdaorm --help.

  • 8b8f470: Stage commands:

  • push/DDL: a stage's last source without condition is a catch-all, as in DML: it gets only the entities no other source took (it used to receive every entity) — L25.

  • fetch/pull on PostgreSQL work with reserved words as column names (order): the metadata query quoted the column twice — L6, L21.
  • stage.fetch() reports the drift: per mapping, the entities that differ from the model (present in one side only, different columns, types, lengths, required, primary key), each with its differences; no entities when in step. stage.read() returns the databases' mappings as fetch did (pull uses it) — L22.

  • cli: lambdaorm fetch exits with code 1 when there are differences (for CI). fetch, pull, schema, introspect and incorporate load the --envfile they declared (it was ignored).

docs.title: Version
docs.text: Prints the version of the CLI that is running and the version of @lambdaorm/lib that the project uses.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). language -l Development language (default: node).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
lambdaorm version

Result (the versions depend on your installation):

lambdaorm cli version: 1.6.10
Local lambdaorm version: 3.5.3

When the project does not depend on @lambdaorm/lib, the second line is Local lambdaorm not found.

To print only the version of the CLI:

lambdaorm --version   # or lambdaorm -v

1.6.10

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Generates the source code of the domain for the development language: the model (model.ts, with the entities and enumerations) and one repository per entity (repository<Entity>.ts). See Repositories.

A repository file is generated only if it does not exist yet, so custom code added to it is kept; the model is regenerated every time.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path. language -l Development language: node (default, uses @lambdaorm/lib) or client-node (uses @lambdaorm/client; the domain is read from the Data Gateway at infrastructure.service.url of the schema, as written by init -u). model -m Builds the model. repositories -r Builds the repositories. all -a Builds the model and the repositories (the default when none of -m, -r, -a is given). src-path Relative path of the source code in the workspace (--src-path). data-path Relative path of the data folder in the workspace (--data-path). domain-path Relative path of the domain in the source code path (--domain-path). url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text: Returns the constraints that are checked when a query expression is executed.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). query -q Query expression. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Drop
docs.text: Removes all the database objects of a stage, but not the database itself. With -o, it prints the statements instead of executing them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Generates the statements but does not apply them. force -f If a statement fails, continue with the next statements. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Execute
docs.text: Executes a query expression and prints its result.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). query -q Query expression. data -d Data (parameters) of the query: JSON, or the path of a JSON file. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Bulk insert
docs.text:
Inserts the countries of a JSON file, with their states:

lambdaorm execute -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -q "Countries.bulkInsert().include(p => p.states)" -d ./lab/countries/countries.json

docs.title: Query
docs.text:
lambdaorm execute -e ".env" -o beautiful -q "Products.distinct(p => ({ quantity: p.quantity, category: p.category.name })).sort(p => p.category).page(1,3)"

Result:

[
  {
    "quantity": "10 boxes x 20 bags",
    "category": "Beverages"
  },
  {
    "quantity": "24 - 12 oz bottles",
    "category": "Beverages"
  },
  {
    "quantity": "12 - 355 ml cans",
    "category": "Beverages"
  }
]

docs.title: On a Data Gateway
docs.text:
lambdaorm execute -u http://gateway:8080/iot/v1 -o beautiful -q "Devices.filter(p => p.status == status)" -d '{"status": "active"}'

With bearer authentication, set the token in the SERVICE_TOKEN environment variable (see the CLI).

docs.title: Export
docs.text: Exports the data of the databases of a stage to a JSON file, <stage>-export.json, in the target folder. The file can be loaded with import.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. target -t Folder where the export file is written (default: the current directory). force -f If a statement fails, continue with the next statements. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Fetch
docs.text:
Shows the drift between the databases of a stage and the model: per mapping, the entities that differ (missing on one side, different columns, types, lengths, nullability or primary key), each with its differences. The entities are empty when the databases are in step with the model. Relations and indexes are not compared.

It exits with code 1 when there are differences, so it can be used in CI.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
lambdaorm fetch -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -o beautiful || echo "the database differs from the model"

Result:

[
  {
    "name": "default",
    "entities": [
      {
        "name": "Countries",
        "mapping": "Countries",
        "differences": ["column phone missing in the database"],
        "properties": [ ... ]
      }
    ]
  }
]

In step:

[
  {
    "name": "default",
    "entities": []
  }
]

docs.title: Import
docs.text: Imports data from a file into the databases of a stage. The file has the format written by export.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. data -d Data to import: the path of a JSON file, or JSON. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Init
docs.text: Generates the structure of a λORM project: the workspace folder and its schema file (lambdaORM.yaml), with a source, a mapping and a stage.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: my-project). source -s Name of the data source. dialect -d Database engine of the project (MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SqlServer, Oracle, MongoDB, SQLjs). Default: MySQL. connection -c Connection string of the database. data-path Relative path of the data folder in the workspace (--data-path). url -u URL of a schema on a Data Gateway: the project is created with the domain of that schema, to be used with the Node.js client.

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text: Returns the metadata of a query expression: its parsed structure.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). query -q Query expression. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Model
docs.text: Returns the model of the result of a query expression: the fields it returns, with their types.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). query -q Query expression. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Returns the parameters of a query expression, with their types.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). query -q Query expression. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text: Returns the execution plan of a query expression: the sentence that runs on each source, without executing it.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). query -q Query expression. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway, to run the command there.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
lambdaorm plan -o beautiful -q "Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).include(p => [p.customer.map(p => p.name), p.details.include(p => p.product.include(p => p.category.map(p => p.name)).map(p => p.name)).map(p => [p.quantity, p.unitPrice])]).page(1,2)"

Result:

{
  "entity": "Orders",
  "dialect": "MongoDB",
  "source": "Ordering",
  "sentence": "[{ \"$match\" : { \"CustomerID\":{{customerId}} } }, { \"$project\" :{ \"_id\": 0 , \"id\":\"$_id\", \"customerId\":\"$CustomerID\", \"employeeId\":\"$EmployeeID\", \"orderDate\":\"$OrderDate\", \"requiredDate\":\"$RequiredDate\", \"shippedDate\":\"$ShippedDate\", \"shipViaId\":\"$ShipVia\", \"freight\":\"$Freight\", \"name\":\"$ShipName\", \"address\":\"$ShipAddress\", \"city\":\"$ShipCity\", \"region\":\"$ShipRegion\", \"postalCode\":\"$ShipPostalCode\", \"country\":\"$ShipCountry\", \"__customerId\":\"$CustomerID\", \"__id\":\"$_id\" ,\"details\": { \"$map\":{ \"input\": \"$\\\"Order Details\\\"\", \"in\": { \"quantity\":\"$$this.Quantity\", \"unitPrice\":\"$$this.UnitPrice\", \"__productId\":\"$$this.ProductID\", \"LambdaOrmParentId\":\"$$this.OrderID\" } }} }} , { \"$sort\" :{ \"_id\":1 } } , { \"$skip\" : 0 }, { \"$limit\" : 2 } , { \"$project\": { \"_id\": 0 } }]",
  "children": [
    {
      "entity": "Customers",
      "dialect": "PostgreSQL",
      "source": "Crm",
      "sentence": "SELECT c.CompanyName AS \"name\", c.CustomerID AS \"LambdaOrmParentId\" FROM Customers c  WHERE  c.CustomerID IN ($1) "
    },
    {
      "entity": "Orders.details",
      "dialect": "MongoDB",
      "source": "Ordering",
      "sentence": "[{ \"$unwind\" : \"$\\\"Order Details\\\"\" }, { \"$replaceRoot\": { \"newRoot\": \"$\\\"Order Details\\\"\" } }, { \"$match\" : { \"OrderID\":{ \"$in\" :[{{LambdaOrmParentId}}]} } }, { \"$project\" :{ \"_id\": 0 , \"quantity\":\"$Quantity\", \"unitPrice\":\"$UnitPrice\", \"__productId\":\"$ProductID\", \"LambdaOrmParentId\":\"$OrderID\" }} , { \"$project\": { \"_id\": 0 } }]",
      "children": [
        {
          "entity": "Products",
          "dialect": "MySQL",
          "source": "Catalog",
          "sentence": "SELECT p.ProductName AS name, p.CategoryID AS `__categoryId`, p.ProductID AS LambdaOrmParentId FROM Products p  WHERE  p.ProductID IN (?) ",
          "children": [
            {
              "entity": "Categories",
              "dialect": "MySQL",
              "source": "Catalog",
              "sentence": "SELECT c1.CategoryName AS name, c1.CategoryID AS LambdaOrmParentId FROM Categories c1  WHERE  c1.CategoryID IN (?) "
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Push
docs.text: Synchronizes the databases of a stage with the model. It compares the model with the databases (what fetch reads), not with the orm_state file: new tables are created with keys, foreign keys and indexes; in existing tables, missing columns are added and columns with another type, length or nullability are altered. It never drops what exists only in the database (fetch reports it). orm_state is still written as a record.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Generates the statements but does not apply them. Without a value, prints them per source; with a folder, writes one script per source that changes, <stage>.<source>.sql. force -f If a statement fails, continue with the next statements.

Note

push runs only locally: it has no -u option.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Apply the changes:

lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env

Write the scripts instead (for example, to keep them as versioned migrations):

lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -s default -o migrations

/home/user/lab/countries/migrations/default.default.sql

Print the statements, per source, without applying them:

lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -o

[
  {
    "source": "default",
    "sentences": [
      "ALTER TABLE Countries ADD phone VARCHAR(20)"
    ]
  }
]

docs.title: Renaming a column
docs.text: To rename a column, set previousMapping in the mapping of the property ({ name: icon, mapping: icon_name, previousMapping: icon }) and remove it once the change is applied. Renaming tables is not supported.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Runs a script: several queries in one transaction. The script is written in 3xpr, and all its orm.execute(query, data, options) calls run in the same transaction, also across sources. The transaction is committed when the script ends and rolled back on any error (a failed query or a throw). The result is the value of the last statement (or of return).

It runs locally with the workspace (-w) or on a Data Gateway (-u, through POST /script); the gateway must have scripts.enabled and the credential must have the script permission.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Description workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). stage -s Name of the stage (default: the first stage of the schema). script -x Script (3xpr statements calling orm.execute(query, data, options)). file -f File with the script (instead of -x). data -d Variables of the script: JSON, or the path of a JSON file. envfile -e Reads a file of environment variables. output -o Output format: json, beautiful, light or yaml. url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway (POST /script).

docs.title: Inline
docs.text:
lambdaorm script -w lab/northwind -e lab/northwind/.env -o beautiful \
  -x 'orm.execute("Orders.update(p => ({ freight: freight })).filter(p => p.id == id)", { id: id, freight: freight }); orm.execute("Orders.filter(p => p.id == id)", { id: id })' \
  -d '{"id": 10248, "freight": 40}'

docs.title: From a file
docs.text:
create-quote.3xpr:

account = orm.execute("Accounts.filter(p => p.id == accountId)", { accountId: accountId });
if (account.length() == 0) { throw { status: 404, message: "account not found" }; }
orm.execute("Quotes.insert()", { id: quoteId, accountId: accountId, status: "draft" });
for (line in lines) {
  orm.execute("QuoteLines.insert()", { id: line.id, quoteId: quoteId, quantity: line.qty });
}
orm.execute("QuoteEvents.insert()", { quoteId: quoteId, event: "created" }, { stage: "insights" });
quoteId

lambdaorm script -w . -f create-quote.3xpr -d quote.json

orm.execute(…, { stage: "insights" }) runs on another stage and joins the same transaction (since @lambdaorm/lib 3.3.0).

docs.title: On a Data Gateway
docs.text:
The URL includes the route of the schema (here crm):

lambdaorm script -u http://localhost:8080/crm -f create-quote.3xpr -d '{"quoteId": 10, "accountId": 1, "lines": []}'

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Language: variables, if / else, for, for … in, while, switch, try / catch, throw, return; there is no ? : operator, no ++ / -- (use i += 1) and no user-defined functions. See Script.
  • The script works on a copy of the data and cannot read environment variables ($VAR fails).
  • Errors are printed as error: …, and nothing the script wrote is kept.
  • With -u, a Data Gateway with bearer authentication needs the token in the SERVICE_TOKEN environment variable of the CLI (sent as Authorization: Bearer; since @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3).
  • The command exits with code 1 when the script fails (since @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3).

docs.title: Sync
docs.text:
The sync command no longer exists: it was replaced by push.

lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env
