docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Give applications, AI agents and people governed access to the data of λORM schemas over the network, by configuration, without writing a backend for it.

A λORM schema already describes a domain (its entities, relations and rules) and where its data lives (one or many databases of different engines). The Data Gateway publishes that schema so that:

  • an application queries and writes it through a REST API (or a WebSocket connection), with the same lambda queries it would use in Node;
  • an AI agent explores the domain and queries it through MCP, knowing the entities and the language;
  • a person explores the schemas, reads each entity as a form, tries queries and draws diagrams in a web UI;

and so that who can do what is decided in one place, the same for all of them: each credential has permissions, and every change is audited.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
What it does:

  • Serves one or several λORM schemas per instance, each at a route (/iot/v1, /iot/v2, /accounts).
  • Exposes them by four transports, each one only when it has a port: REST (http), MCP (mcpHttp, mcpWebSocket) and a JSON-RPC API over WebSocket (webSocket).
  • Every operation of λORM: queries (execute, plan, metadata, model, parameters, constraints), scripts (several queries in one transaction), queued executions (Kafka), the schema and its model, and stages (export, import).
  • Authentication (API key, bearer token, basic) and permissions per credential (read, write, script, queue, stageImport), globally, per transport or per schema.
  • Isolation: each schema runs in its own worker, with its own environment and connections; one that fails doesn't affect the others.
  • Audit of writes, metrics (Prometheus), health (Kubernetes probes), limits (rate, concurrency, sizes, time).
  • A web UI: explorer, entity forms, query tabs with autocompletion, saved queries and diagrams of the domain.

What it doesn't do:

  • It doesn't define the domain nor migrate the databases: that is the schema and the CLI (push, pull, …).
  • It doesn't accept SQL: only λORM queries, translated for each source.
  • No users nor roles of its own beyond the credentials of its configuration (no login against an identity provider yet).
  • The UI keeps what is saved in each browser; there is no shared storage of saved queries on the server.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The Data Gateway is a Node application published as the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway. It reads one configuration file (data-gateway.config.yaml) that says where the schemas are, how they are exposed and who can use them; the schemas themselves stay in their λORM workspaces (lambdaORM.yaml).

Inside, a supervisor starts and watches the workers. The edge worker listens on the ports of the transports, authenticates each request and sends it, by a direct channel, to the worker of the schema, which checks the permissions, runs the operation with λORM against its databases and audits it. A heavy query in one schema doesn't slow down another; a schema whose database is down answers 503 and is retried, while the others keep working.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Concept What it is Schema a λORM workspace (a folder with lambdaORM.yaml): domain, sources, mappings, stages; served at a route Route where a schema is reached: /iot/v1/execute, /iot/v1/mcp, ws://host/iot/v1; a single schema can be at the root Transport a way in, on its own port: http, mcpHttp, mcpWebSocket, webSocket Credential a key, token or user with a name and permissions; sent by the client in each request Permission read, write, script, queue, stageImport: what the credential can do, on every transport Stage a λORM scenario of a schema (which sources hold which entities); chosen with options.stage Worker where a schema runs: a thread or a process of its own

docs.title: A request, step by step
docs.text:
1. A client sends POST /iot/v1/execute with X-Api-Key: … and { "query": "Orders.filter(…)", "data": {…} }.
  2. The http transport finds the credential (agent, permissions [read]) and the schema iot/v1.
  3. The schema's worker analyses the query: it only selects, so read is enough.
  4. λORM translates it for each source of the stage, runs it and joins the results.
  5. The answer goes back as JSON. Had it written data, the credential would have needed write, and the operation would have left an audit line.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
• Getting started: step by step, from an empty folder to the REST API, the UI, MCP and WebSocket.
  • Configuration: the configuration file, schemas, environment, runtime and every key.
  • Transports: the four transports, their routes and options.
  • REST API: every method of the http transport, with examples.
  • MCP: the tools, resources and transports for AI agents.
  • WebSocket API: the JSON-RPC methods and the notifications.
  • Security: authentication, permissions, audit, limits and errors.
  • UI: the web interface: explorer, entity forms, queries, saved queries and diagrams.
  • Clients: @lambdaorm/client, the CLI and the OpenAPI document.
  • Operations: Docker, Kubernetes, health, metrics and logs.
  • Change log

docs.title: 3.0.0-rc.4 (2026-11-18)
docs.text:
Prerelease: it doesn't move latest. Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.3.

Bug Fixes:

  • Swagger (/doc): Authorize offers the credential the served schemas are configured with (an API key in its header, a bearer token or basic); it offered a fixed bearer token, so it didn't work with an API key. Each http transport serves its own document.
  • From @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.3: a PostgreSQL bytea column is read as buffer (lambdaorm pull, fetch and introspect failed with error with type: bytea), and a buffer property is created as BYTEA.

docs.title: 3.0.0-rc.3 (2026-11-18)
docs.text:
Prerelease: it doesn't move latest. Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.2.

Features (the UI at /ui, built on @lambdaorm/ui):

  • Named Data Gateway: a home page with what it is and the schemas, a login page (show / hide the secret) and the query page, with logout; the theme (system / light / dark) and the language (English, Español, Português, Français, Italiano, Deutsch, Nederlands, Català, Galego, Euskara) are chosen at the top and kept in the browser. The credential is never kept.
  • An explorer of the schemas on the left. For each schema: its domain as YAML, read only (only GET /{schema}/domain: never the sources nor the connections); its entities with their properties and relations, and the form of each entity (properties, relations and references, keys, indexes and constraints, rows read only by pages, diagram).
  • Folders, queries and diagrams saved with a name and a description, moved by dragging; queries in tabs with Save, Save as… and Ctrl+S. Saved diagrams: the chosen entities laid out by themselves, boxes and lines moved by hand, boxes taken out with their ×, the names of the relations, export to SVG and PNG.
  • What is saved stays in the browser (IndexedDB, per gateway and user of the credential) and is exported to and imported from a JSON file.
  • Results: a copy icon and an export menu (JSON, YAML, tab-separated text).
  • The Swagger page says Data Gateway and the version of the instance.

docs.title: 3.0.0-rc.2 (2026-11-18)
docs.text:
Prerelease: it doesn't move latest.

Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.2.

Bug Fixes (from @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.1 / 3.5.2):

  • like(p.name, 'Ch%') with the pattern written in the query, p.name.includes('ch') ("contains"), and startsWith / includes with the value in a variable work on every SQL engine.
  • The date functions (year, month, day, addDay, dayDiff, …) on a column work on PostgreSQL.
  • The MCP guide (lambdaorm://guide/expressions) and the description of orm_execute teach them; the evaluation set has two more questions (contains, like with _).

docs.title: 3.0.0-rc.1 (2026-11-18)
docs.text:
First release of the Data Gateway, published as the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway. Prerelease: it doesn't move latest. Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.0.

Features:

  • One mandatory configuration file (DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH, default /config/data-gateway.config.yaml), with environment variables anywhere in it.
  • Transports by configuration, each on its own port, none by default: http (the REST API), mcpHttp (MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless or stateful, plus the deprecated HTTP+SSE), mcpWebSocket and webSocket (JSON-RPC with notifications).
  • MCP: 22 tools (one per operation, writes included) listed by the credential's permissions, with readOnlyHint / destructiveHint, the domain in the description of orm_execute, resources (lambdaorm://guide/expressions, the domain, each entity) and mcp.maxRows.
  • Several schemas: discovered under orm.workspacePath (the folder is the route: /iot/v1) and declared in orm.schemas, with overrides per schema (transports, authentication, env, scripts, mcp, server, runtime). Each schema worker receives only its own variables.
  • Runtime: a supervisor, an edge worker with the transports and a worker per schema (thread or process); heartbeat, restarts with a growing wait, server.maxConcurrent (429) and server.maxResponseBytes (413). A schema that doesn't start or falls doesn't affect the others; at start each schema checks a connection of each source.
  • Credentials with permissions (read, write, script, queue, stageImport) for bearer, API key and basic; a write with only read is refused before connecting.
  • Audit of writes, scripts, queued executions and stage imports (a JSON line "type":"audit" on stdout).
  • The query UI at /ui (transports.http.ui.enabled, off by default), built on @lambdaorm/ui; GET /typings and GET /whoami per schema.
  • Metrics of every worker in /metrics (and /{schema}/metrics); logs labeled by worker.
  • The image runs node index.js (it stops on SIGTERM).

Known limits (of @lambdaorm/lib, avoided by the MCP guide): like with a literal pattern, includes over text, grouping by an expression, the sql.js adapter. Fixed in rc.2.

docs.title: Node: @lambdaorm/client
docs.text:
@lambdaorm/client has the same interface as the library (orm.execute, orm.plan, orm.executeScript, …) and runs it on a Data Gateway. The URL includes the schema's route; http(s):// uses the REST API and ws(s):// the WebSocket API.

npm install @lambdaorm/client

import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/client'

// REST, an API key
await orm.init('http://gateway:8080/iot/v1', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': process.env.IOT_KEY } })
const devices = await orm.execute('Devices.filter(p => p.status == status)', { status: 'active' })

// a bearer token: sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>
await orm.init('http://gateway:8080/iot/v1', { token: process.env.IOT_TOKEN })

Over WebSocket, every operation uses one persistent connection, and orm.on receives the notifications (queue.completed, queue.failed, schema.statusChanged):

await orm.init('ws://gateway:8083/iot/v1', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': process.env.IOT_KEY } })
const stop = orm.on('schema.statusChanged', state => console.log(state.path, state.status, state.reason))
const products = await orm.execute('Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice)', { minPrice: 50 })
// …
stop()
await orm.end()     // closes the connection

With a single schema at the root, the URL is the gateway's: http://gateway:8080.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The CLI runs its commands locally with a workspace (-w) or on a Data Gateway with -u and the schema's URL. With bearer authentication, the token is taken from the SERVICE_TOKEN environment variable:

export SERVICE_TOKEN=…
lambdaorm execute -q "Devices.filter(p => p.status == 'active')" -u http://gateway:8080/iot/v1
lambdaorm script -x "orm.execute(\"Devices.map(p => count(1))\")" -u http://gateway:8080/iot/v1

docs.title: Other languages
docs.text: The OpenAPI 3 document of the REST API is served by the gateway (/doc, /api-docs): a client for any language can be generated from it with OpenAPI Generator.

docs.title: AI agents
docs.text:
Through MCP:

claude mcp add --transport http iot-v1 http://gateway:8081/iot/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: $KEY"

docs.title: Web
docs.text: The UI of the gateway, and @lambdaorm/ui to put it in an application of your own.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Everything is configured in one YAML file, mounted in the container, never baked into the image:

  • Path: DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH (default /config/data-gateway.config.yaml). It is mandatory: without it the gateway logs the error and exits with code 1. An invalid key or value also stops the start, with the list of problems.
  • $VAR and ${VAR} are replaced by environment variables anywhere in the file, also inside a text ("${HOST}:${PORT}"). A variable that is not defined counts as not set: a transport whose port: $VAR is not defined is not exposed; a credential whose secret is not defined stops the start.
  • The λORM schemas (lambdaORM.yaml, sources, mappings, stages, queue) stay in their workspaces. The gateway's file says where they are, how each one is reached and how it is exposed.

docs.title: Transports and ports
docs.text:
A transport is exposed only when it has a port. There are no default ports, neither in the code nor in the image:

transports.<name> Result missing not exposed present without port, or port: $VAR with the variable not defined not exposed (logged: mcpHttp not exposed: no port configured) port that is not an integer 1–65535 configuration error: the gateway doesn't start two transports on the same host:port configuration error no transport exposed at all configuration error

So the same file can expose MCP only where DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_PORT is defined. The transports are described in Transports.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
A schema is a λORM workspace (a folder with lambdaORM.yaml) served at a route (iot/v1). They are declared in two ways, which can be combined.

Discovered (orm.workspacePath). The folder is walked at start: every folder with a lambdaORM.yaml is a schema and its relative path is its route. Below a schema the walk stops (a workspace has folders of its own).

/workspace                          (orm.workspacePath)
├── iot/
│   ├── v1/lambdaORM.yaml    →  schema "iot/v1"       →  /iot/v1/...
│   └── v2/lambdaORM.yaml    →  schema "iot/v2"       →  /iot/v2/...
└── accounts/
    └── v1/lambdaORM.yaml    →  schema "accounts/v1"  →  /accounts/v1/...

Declared (orm.schemas[] with workspace). The route doesn't depend on where the folder is: one volume per schema, or an instance that serves only some schemas.

orm:
  workspacePath: /workspace
  schemas:
    - path: accounts/v1
      workspace: /mnt/accounts          # a folder with lambdaORM.yaml, or the file itself

Adjusted. An entry of orm.schemas[] without workspace adjusts a discovered schema (its path must match one). What a schema can adjust:

Key of a schema Effect If not set transports the transports that expose it; on the others its routes don't exist (404) every exposed transport authentication replaces the authentication (and its permissions) for this schema, on all its transports the transport's, else the global one env variables its worker receives (below) its .env and the base variables scripts enabled and the limits of scripts scripts mcp.maxRows, mcp.tools row limit and tools of its MCP server mcp server.timeout, server.maxConcurrent, server.maxResponseBytes timeout, simultaneous operations and response size server runtime.mode, runtime.maxMemoryMb, runtime.checkConnections thread / process, memory of its worker, whether its connections are checked at start runtime

The most specific always wins and replaces the others: schema → transport → global.

Rules:

  • At least one of orm.workspacePath or a orm.schemas[] with workspace, and at least one schema.
  • Two schemas with the same route, or a route that is the prefix of another (iot and iot/v1), are an error.
  • Each segment of a route: [a-zA-Z0-9_.-], and none of the reserved names: health, ping, metrics, version, schemas, mcp, sse, messages, status, doc, api-docs, swagger, asyncapi, ui, whoami, typings.
  • A schema at the root: if workspacePath itself has a lambdaORM.yaml (or a declared schema uses path: ""), it is served at the root (/execute). Only when it is the only schema.
  • No hot reload: a new schema is taken when the gateway restarts.
  • Each schema uses the infrastructure.queue (Kafka) of its own lambdaORM.yaml, if it has one.

docs.title: Environment of each schema
docs.text:
λORM replaces the $VAR of a lambdaORM.yaml with the environment. So that a schema cannot read another one's credentials nor the gateway's secrets, each schema worker receives only its own variables, from highest to lowest priority:

Source Example schemas[].env in the gateway's file (the values can use the gateway's variables) DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB a .env file in the schema's workspace (optional) /workspace/iot/v1/.env the base variables: PATH, HOME, TZ, LANG, NODE_*, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, ORACLE_*, and runtime.env.passthrough TZ=UTC

Every lambdaORM.yaml can use the same names, and the gateway maps each one to its real secret:

orm:
  workspacePath: /workspace
  schemas:
    - path: iot/v1
      env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB }
    - path: iot/v2
      env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V2_DB }      # iot/v2 can be an exact copy of iot/v1
runtime:
  env:
    isolate: true                           # false: every schema gets the whole environment (local development)
    passthrough: [ KAFKA_BROKER ]           # variables every schema receives

A variable used in schemas[].env that is not defined stays undefined: that schema fails to connect and is shown in error with the reason; the others start.

docs.title: Runtime
docs.text:
runtime:
  schemas: thread           # thread | process: one worker per schema (runtime.mode adjusts one schema)
  maxMemoryMb: 512          # JavaScript heap of each worker; above it, only that worker is restarted
  checkConnections: true    # at start each schema opens a connection of each source: a database down → error, retried
  threadpoolSize: auto      # UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE; auto = max(4, 2 × schemas in thread mode), at most 64
  heartbeat:
    intervalMs: 5000
    timeoutMs: 30000        # a worker that doesn't answer is ended and restarted
  restart:
    initialDelayMs: 1000    # first wait before retrying a fallen worker or a schema that didn't start
    maxDelayMs: 300000      # the wait grows up to this
  env: { isolate: true, passthrough: [] }

What each mode isolates:

thread process another instance CPU and event loop yes yes yes JavaScript heap (maxMemoryMb) yes yes yes A hung worker (heartbeat) yes yes yes Environment variables yes yes yes libuv thread pool (DNS, fs, native drivers) shared (threadpoolSize) yes yes Native memory, container OOM no same container yes A crash of native code no: the whole process yes yes

thread suits development and small schemas; runtime.mode: process a critical schema in production (Oracle in thick mode uses native code); a separate instance, schemas of different teams or customers.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
# data-gateway.config.yaml
orm:
  workspacePath: /workspace
  schemas:
    - path: iot/v1                      # discovered: only adjustments
      transports: [ http ]              # not exposed by MCP
      env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB }
      scripts: { enabled: false }
    - path: iot/v2
      env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V2_DB }
      mcp: { maxRows: 100 }
      runtime: { maxMemoryMb: 1024 }
    - path: accounts/v1                 # declared: defines and adjusts
      workspace: /mnt/accounts
      env: { DB_CONNECTION: $ACCOUNTS_DB }
      runtime: { mode: process }
      authentication:
        adapter: local
        type: apikey
        keys:
          - { name: accounts-backend, value: $ACCOUNTS_KEY, permissions: [ read, write ] }

runtime:
  schemas: thread
  maxMemoryMb: 512

server:
  timeout: 120000                  # ms per request, message or tool call
  maxConcurrent: 64                # simultaneous operations per schema; above it, 429
  requestBodySize: 14MB
  maxResponseBytes: 256MB          # 0 = no limit

logger: { adapter: console, level: info }
metrics: { enabled: true }
audit: { enabled: true, includeData: false }

authentication:                    # for every schema and transport that doesn't set its own
  adapter: local
  type: apikey
  header: X-Api-Key
  keys:
    - { name: agent,   value: $AGENT_KEY,   permissions: [ read ] }
    - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_KEY, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] }

rateLimit: { windowMs: 30000, max: 0 }   # http only; max: 0 = no rate limit

scripts: { enabled: true, maxLength: 20000, timeoutMs: 30000, maxIterations: 100000 }

mcp:
  name: data-gateway
  tools: { include: [], exclude: [] }
  pageSize: 50
  maxRows: 500

transports:
  http:
    port: $DATA_GATEWAY_HTTP_PORT
    ui: { enabled: true }
  mcpHttp:
    port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_HTTP_PORT
  mcpWebSocket:
    port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_WS_PORT
  webSocket:
    port: $DATA_GATEWAY_WS_PORT

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: Key Default Notes orm.workspacePath — the folder where schemas are discovered orm.schemas[] [] path (mandatory), workspace (defines a schema) and adjustments runtime.schemas thread thread / process runtime.maxMemoryMb 512 per worker runtime.checkConnections true a database down leaves the schema in error, retried, instead of failing in the first query runtime.threadpoolSize auto max(4, 2 × schemas in thread mode), at most 64 runtime.heartbeat.intervalMs / timeoutMs 5000 / 30000 runtime.restart.initialDelayMs / maxDelayMs 1000 / 300000 growing wait between restarts runtime.env.isolate / passthrough true / [] server.timeout 120000 per HTTP request, WebSocket message and MCP tool call server.maxConcurrent 64 simultaneous operations per schema; above it 429; 0 = no limit server.requestBodySize 14MB server.maxResponseBytes 256MB above it, 413; 0 = no limit logger.adapter / logger.level console / info console or winston; error, warn, info, debug metrics.enabled true audit.enabled true the audit of writes (Security) audit.includeData false true adds the parameters (data), which can have personal data authentication { adapter: none } Security transports.<t>.authentication authentication replaces the global one for that transport rateLimit.windowMs / rateLimit.max 30000 / 30 http only; max: 0 turns it off scripts.enabled false POST /script and its tool and method scripts.maxLength / timeoutMs / maxIterations 20000 / 30000 / 100000 a request can ask for less, never more mcp.name data-gateway the name of the MCP servers; each one adds its route mcp.tools.include / exclude [] / [] names of tools mcp.pageSize 50 page of tools/list and resources/list mcp.maxRows 500 rows of orm_execute / orm_execute_script; 0 = no limit transports.<t>.port none without a port, the transport is not exposed transports.<t>.host 0.0.0.0 transports.<t>.basePath '' a prefix before the schema's route (/data-gateway), behind an ingress with a path transports.<t>.maxConnections 100 webSocket, mcpWebSocket and the SSE of mcpHttp transports.http.swagger.enabled true /doc and /api-docs transports.http.ui.enabled false the UI at /ui transports.mcpHttp.legacySse true besides Streamable HTTP, the older HTTP+SSE for older clients transports.mcpHttp.stateful false stateless Streamable HTTP: any replica answers any request transports.<ws>.asyncapi.enabled true GET /asyncapi and /asyncapi.json of webSocket and mcpWebSocket

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This guide goes from an empty folder to the northwind database published by a Data Gateway: its REST API, its web UI, MCP for an AI agent and its WebSocket API. It takes about ten minutes and needs only Docker (with Docker Compose).

docs.title: 1. The files
docs.text:
Create a folder with this layout (the files can be downloaded from this wiki):

northwind/
├── docker-compose.yml          ← PostgreSQL and the Data Gateway
├── data-gateway.config.yaml    ← how the gateway exposes the schema and who can use it
├── data.json                   ← the rows of northwind, to import
└── workspace/
    └── lambdaORM.yaml          ← the λORM schema: domain, mapping, source, stage

mkdir -p northwind/workspace && cd northwind
W=https://lambda-orm.github.io/wiki/data-gateway/northwind
curl -sO $W/docker-compose.yml
curl -sO $W/data-gateway.config.yaml
curl -sO $W/data.json
curl -s $W/lambdaORM.yaml -o workspace/lambdaORM.yaml

docs.title: The schema: workspace/lambdaORM.yaml
docs.text:
A normal λORM schema: the domain (entities, properties, relations), the mapping to the tables, one source (PostgreSQL) and the stage default. An excerpt:

domain:
  entities:
  - name: Products
    primaryKey: ["id"]
    uniqueKey: ["name", "supplierId"]
    properties:
    - { name: id, type: integer, required: true, autoIncrement: true }
    - { name: name, required: true }
    - { name: categoryId, type: integer }
    - { name: price, type: decimal, default: 0 }
    relations:
    - { name: category, from: categoryId, entity: Categories, to: id, target: products }
  # … Categories, Customers, Orders, Orders.details
infrastructure:
  mappings:
  - name: default
    entities:
    - name: Products
      mapping: Products
      properties:
      - { name: id, mapping: ProductID }
      - { name: name, mapping: ProductName }
      # …
  sources:
  - name: Northwind
    dialect: PostgreSQL
    mapping: default
    connection: ${NORTHWIND_DB}      # an environment variable: the gateway gives it to this schema
  stages:
  - name: default
    sources:
    - name: Northwind

docs.title: The gateway: data-gateway.config.yaml
docs.text:
orm:
  workspacePath: /workspace            # the folder with lambdaORM.yaml (a single schema: served at the root)
  schemas:
    - path: ""                         # that schema: it receives only the variables given here
      env: { NORTHWIND_DB: $NORTHWIND_DB }
authentication:
  adapter: local
  type: apikey
  header: X-Api-Key
  keys:
    - { name: reader,  value: $READER_KEY,  permissions: [ read ] }
    - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_KEY, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] }
scripts:
  enabled: true
transports:
  http:
    port: 8080
    ui: { enabled: true }
  mcpHttp:
    port: 8081
  webSocket:
    port: 8083
  • Two credentials: reader can only read; backend can also write, run scripts, queue and import.
  • Three transports: REST and the UI on 8080, MCP on 8081, WebSocket on 8083.
  • The variables of the schema: each schema receives only its own variables, for its safety; env gives it the connection.

docs.title: docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: northwind
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: northwind
      POSTGRES_DB: northwind
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "northwind" ]
      interval: 2s
      retries: 30

  data-gateway:
    image: flaviorita/data-gateway:3.0.0-rc.4
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      NORTHWIND_DB: '{"host":"postgres","port":5432,"user":"northwind","password":"northwind","database":"northwind"}'
      READER_KEY: ${READER_KEY:-reader-demo-key}
      BACKEND_KEY: ${BACKEND_KEY:-backend-demo-key}
    volumes:
      - ./data-gateway.config.yaml:/config/data-gateway.config.yaml:ro
      - ./workspace:/workspace
    ports:
      - "${HTTP_PORT:-8080}:8080"
      - "${MCP_PORT:-8081}:8081"
      - "${WS_PORT:-8083}:8083"

The keys reader-demo-key and backend-demo-key are for this example only: in any real use, give READER_KEY and BACKEND_KEY long random values (openssl rand -hex 24).

docs.title: 2. Start it
docs.text:
docker compose up -d
curl http://localhost:8080/schemas

[ { "path": "", "status": "ready", "since": "2026-11-18T14:07:33.561Z", "restarts": 0 } ]

The schema is ready: it is served at the root (/execute, /mcp, …). If it says error, reason tells why (a database that can't be reached, a variable not given); the gateway keeps retrying.

docs.title: 3. Create the tables
docs.text:
The image includes the λORM CLI. push creates the tables of the stage from the schema:

docker compose exec data-gateway lambdaorm push -w /workspace -s default

create table Categories
…
add foreign key Order Details_product_FK

docs.title: 4. Import the data, through the REST API
docs.text:
The import needs the stageImport permission, so reader can't:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json

{ "error": "ForbiddenError", "message": "the credential \"reader\" does not have the \"stageImport\" permission" }

and backend can (it answers 204, and the import leaves an audit line in the log):

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: backend-demo-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json
docker compose logs data-gateway | grep '"type":"audit"'

{"type":"audit","time":"2026-11-18T14:07:39.720Z","schema":"","transport":"http","credential":"backend","operation":"stageImport","stage":"default","durationMs":189,"result":"ok"}

docs.title: 5. Query
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/execute?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice).map(p => ({ name: p.name, category: p.category.name, price: p.price })).sort(p => desc(p.price)).page(1, 3)",
    "data": { "minPrice": 50 }
  }'

[
  { "name": "Côte de Blaye", "category": "Beverages", "price": 263.5 },
  { "name": "Thüringer Rostbratwurst", "category": "Meat/Poultry", "price": 123.79 },
  { "name": "Mishi Kobe Niku", "category": "Meat/Poultry", "price": 97 }
]

p.category.name follows the relation: λORM joins Categories. plan shows how, without running it:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/plan?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice).map(p => ({ name: p.name, category: p.category.name, price: p.price })).sort(p => desc(p.price)).page(1, 3)"}'

{
  "entity": "Products",
  "dialect": "PostgreSQL",
  "source": "Northwind",
  "sentence": "SELECT p.ProductName AS \"name\", c.CategoryName AS \"category\", p.UnitPrice AS \"price\" FROM Products p INNER JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice > $1 ORDER BY p.UnitPrice desc  OFFSET 0 LIMIT 3 "
}

docs.title: 6. Write, and the permissions
docs.text:
A query that writes, with reader:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Products.update(p => ({ price: price })).filter(p => p.id == id)", "data": {"id": 38, "price": 270}}'

{ "error": "ForbiddenError", "message": "the credential \"reader\" does not have the \"write\" permission" }

The gateway refused it before reaching the database, because the query is not a select. With backend it answers the rows updated, 1, and leaves an audit line.

docs.title: 7. A script: several queries in one transaction
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/script?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: backend-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "script": "orders = orm.execute(\"Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).map(p => p.id)\", { customerId: customerId }); { customer: customerId, orders: orders.length() }",
  "data": { "customerId": "ALFKI" }
}'

{ "customer": "ALFKI", "orders": 6 }

A script chooses the status of the answer with throw { status, message }: a customer not found with status: 404 answers 404. See Script.

docs.title: 8. The API documentation
docs.text: http://localhost:8080/doc/ is the Swagger UI of the REST API. Authorize asks for the API key in the X-Api-Key header; then every method can be tried from the page.

docs.title: 9. The UI
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:8080/ui/:

Login with the API key (the Show button shows what was typed):

On the left, the explorer: the schema, its domain, its entities with their properties and relations. Choose the schema /, write a query (the editor completes the entities and properties as you type), its data, and execute (Ctrl+Enter). The result can be seen as a table, tree, JSON or YAML, copied and exported:

Save it with Ctrl+S: a name, a description and a folder (folders are created with the + of the schema):

A double click on an entity (or its Open button) shows its form: properties, relations, keys and indexes, its rows and its diagram.

A diagram: the + of a folder → New diagram, choose Orders and Add their neighbours:

The boxes are laid out by themselves; they and the lines can be dragged, and Save keeps them where they were left:

Everything is explained in UI.

docs.title: 10. An AI agent, through MCP
docs.text:
With Claude Code:

claude mcp add --transport http northwind http://localhost:8081/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key"

Then ask it, for example, "how many products does each category have?". The agent sees the tools the reader credential can use (orm_execute, orm_plan, schema_domain, …; not the ones that write), with the domain of northwind in their descriptions, and answers with a query like:

{ "name": "orm_execute", "arguments": { "query": "Categories.map(p => ({ category: p.name, products: count(p.products.id) }))" } }

[ { "category": "Grains/Cereals", "products": 7 }, { "category": "Beverages", "products": 12 }, … ]

With reader, the agent cannot change anything, whatever it is asked. See MCP.

docs.title: 11. WebSocket
docs.text:
One connection for every operation, with notifications. With @lambdaorm/client:

import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/client'

await orm.init('ws://localhost:8083/', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': 'reader-demo-key' } })
const customers = await orm.execute('Customers.filter(p => p.country == country).map(p => p.name)', { country: 'Argentina' })
// [ { name: 'Cactus Comidas para llevar' }, { name: 'Océano Atlántico Ltda.' }, { name: 'Rancho grande' } ]
await orm.end()

or the JSON-RPC messages themselves:

→ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "query.execute", "params": { "query": "Customers.filter(p => p.country == country).map(p => p.name)", "data": { "country": "Argentina" } } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": [ { "name": "Cactus Comidas para llevar" }, { "name": "Océano Atlántico Ltda." }, { "name": "Rancho grande" } ] }

See WebSocket API.

docs.title: 12. Stop it
docs.text: docker compose down            # keeps nothing: the database is in the container

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Several schemas, one route each, and the environment of each: Configuration.
  • Credentials per schema or per transport, the audit, the limits: Security.
  • Every REST method: REST API. Production: Operations.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text:
The gateway is a Model Context Protocol server, so AI agents (Claude Code and any MCP client) can explore the domain and query the data with λORM's language. There is one MCP server per schema (/iot/v1/mcp): its tools describe that schema's domain, and each version is registered as a separate server in the client (iot-v1, iot-v2).

claude mcp add --transport http iot-v1 http://localhost:8081/iot/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: $KEY"

With a single schema at the root: http://localhost:8081/mcp.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
One tool per operation of the schema, writes included: an agent can do what an application does, if its credential allows it. The descriptions and input schemas are generated when the schema starts and carry its domain (entities, properties, relations, enums), so the model knows what to query without a previous call.

Tool Arguments REST equivalent Permission Hint orm_execute query, data?, options? POST /execute read (selects) or write read only with read; destructive with write orm_execute_script script, data?, options? POST /script script destructive orm_execute_queued topic, query, data?, chunk?, options? POST /execute-queued queue destructive orm_plan query, options? POST /plan read read only orm_metadata query POST /metadata read read only orm_model query POST /model read read only orm_parameters query POST /parameters read read only orm_constraints query POST /constraints read read only schema_get — GET /schema read read only schema_version — GET /schema/version read read only schema_domain — GET /domain read read only schema_entities entity? GET /entities[/{entity}] read read only schema_enums enum? GET /enums[/{enum}] read read only schema_sources source? GET /sources[/{source}] read read only schema_mappings mapping?, entity? GET /mappings… read read only schema_views — GET /views read read only schema_stages stage? GET /stages[/{stage}] read read only stage_exists stage GET /stages/{stage}/exists read read only stage_export stage GET /stages/{stage}/export read read only stage_import stage, data POST /stages/{stage}/import stageImport destructive gateway_version — GET /version read read only gateway_health — GET /health read read only
  • tools/list shows a credential only the tools it can use. Without script, orm_execute_script doesn't appear; with only read, orm_execute is described as "read-only queries with this credential".
  • The hints (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) don't block anything: they tell the client which tools change data, so it can ask for confirmation. What blocks is the permissions.
  • The same rules as REST: orm_execute_script fails if scripts are disabled; orm_execute_queued, if the schema has no queue.
  • mcp.tools.include / exclude (global or per schema) restrict the list further, for example exclude: [ orm_execute_script, stage_import ].

docs.title: Results and errors
docs.text:
• A result is { content: [{ type: "text", text: <JSON> }] }, with structuredContent too when it is small.
  • Row limit (mcp.maxRows, default 500). When orm_execute or orm_execute_script answer a longer list, it is cut and the model is told how to ask for less:
{ "rows": [ "…500 rows…" ], "truncated": true, "returned": 500, "total": 18234,
  "hint": "The result was cut to 500 rows. Use .page(1, 500) (or a smaller page), aggregate with map/count, or filter the query more." }

It applies only to MCP and after the query ran: it protects the model's context. The database is protected by server.maxResponseBytes and server.timeout. - An error of λORM (syntax, an unknown entity, a constraint, a disabled script) or a missing permission answers isError: true with the message, so the model can read it and correct the query.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: URI Content lambdaorm://guide/expressions a short guide of the query language (Markdown), to give the model context lambdaorm://schema/domain the whole domain of the schema, JSON lambdaorm://entities/{entity} one entity (template)

docs.title: What an agent can do
docs.text: There is no read-only mode of the transport: what an agent can do is decided by its credential's permissions. An agent that only queries gets a credential with [ read ]: it can run selects but not write, run scripts, queue or import, by any transport. Besides: schemas[].transports to keep a schema out of MCP, mcp.tools.exclude, the hints, and the permissions of the database user (the guarantee underneath). Every write an agent makes is audited with the name of its credential and "transport": "mcpHttp".

docs.title: mcpHttp
docs.text:
Route Protocol POST/GET/DELETE {basePath}/{schema}/mcp Streamable HTTP: Claude Code --transport http and current clients GET {basePath}/{schema}/sse + POST {basePath}/{schema}/messages?sessionId=<id> HTTP+SSE (deprecated), with legacySse: true GET {basePath}/status the state of the transport, the schemas and the open SSE sessions

Streamable HTTP is stateless by default (stateful: false): each POST stands alone and any replica answers it. The credential goes in every request.

docs.title: mcpWebSocket
docs.text:
An upgrade at {basePath}/{schema}/mcp, authenticated in the handshake; JSON-RPC 2.0 messages with the MCP methods (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, …). It is not a standard MCP transport: it is offered for clients and gateways that support it on their own. Its AsyncAPI document is at GET {basePath}/asyncapi.

→ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "orm_execute", "arguments": { "query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > 50).map(p => p.name)" } } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "[\"Côte de Blaye\", \"Thüringer Rostbratwurst\"]" } ] } }

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The image is flaviorita/data-gateway: Node 24, the lambdaorm CLI and the Oracle Instant Client. It runs node index.js as the user 1000, reads the configuration from /config/data-gateway.config.yaml (DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH) and the workspaces from where the configuration says (/workspace by convention). It has no EXPOSE: the ports are only in the configuration.

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  data-gateway:
    image: flaviorita/data-gateway:3.0.0-rc.4
    environment:
      DATA_GATEWAY_HTTP_PORT: "8080"
      DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_PORT: "8081"
      READER_KEY: ${READER_KEY}
      BACKEND_KEY: ${BACKEND_KEY}
      NORTHWIND_DB: ${NORTHWIND_DB}
    volumes:
      - ./data-gateway.config.yaml:/config/data-gateway.config.yaml:ro
      - ./workspace:/workspace:ro
    ports: [ "8080:8080", "8081:8081" ]
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))" ]
      interval: 10s
      retries: 6

The versions 3.0.0-rc.* are prereleases: they don't move latest.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
• Probes: livenessProbe on GET /ping (the gateway is up), readinessProbe on GET /health (200 while some schema is ready). A probe per schema: GET /{schema}/health.
  • Configuration in a ConfigMap mounted at /config, secrets as environment variables from a Secret (value: $READER_KEY in the file).
  • Replicas: REST, WebSocket and stateless MCP (stateful: false) need no session affinity; the older HTTP+SSE of MCP does.
  • Behind an ingress with a path: transports.<t>.basePath: /data-gateway.
  • Shutdown: SIGTERM stops accepting connections, waits for the operations in progress (up to server.timeout), closes the queues and the pools, and exits. Give terminationGracePeriodSeconds at least that time.

docs.title: Health
docs.text:
Route Answers GET /ping { "message": "pong", "time" }: the gateway answers GET /health 200 while some schema is ready, 503 if none GET /schemas each schema with status (starting, ready, error, restarting), reason, since and restarts GET /{schema}/health 200 when that schema is ready, 503 if not GET /status in mcpHttp and mcpWebSocket: the state of the transport

A schema in error is retried with a growing wait (runtime.restart) and goes back to ready when its database does, without restarting anything else.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
GET /metrics answers the metrics of every worker in Prometheus format (GET /{schema}/metrics, those of one schema), each with the label worker (edge, schema:iot/v1):

Metric Labels data_gateway_requests_total transport, schema, method, status, credential data_gateway_request_duration_seconds transport, schema, method data_gateway_forbidden_total credential, permission data_gateway_throttled_total schema, transport (answers 429 by maxConcurrent) data_gateway_connections transport data_gateway_schema_status schema, status data_gateway_schema_restarts schema data_gateway_event_loop_lag_seconds worker

and the usual metrics of Node (memory, CPU, event loop). metrics.enabled: false turns them off.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Each worker logs with its label ([supervisor], [edge], [schema:iot/v1]): the start, the transports exposed or not, the effective configuration without secrets, the states of the schemas, falls and restarts, heartbeats missed, and every operation with the name of its credential (never its secret). logger.level: error, warn, info, debug; logger.adapter: console or winston.

The audit of writes goes to the standard output as JSON lines with "type": "audit", to be kept apart by the log collector.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: The http transport (Transports) exposes every operation of λORM on a schema as REST, with JSON in and out. The OpenAPI 3 document is served by the gateway at /doc (Swagger UI) and /api-docs.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
The examples use a gateway at http://localhost:8080 with an API key. Each schema's methods are under its route:

Gateway Schema iot/v1 Only schema at the root http://localhost:8080 http://localhost:8080/iot/v1/execute http://localhost:8080/execute

With transports.http.basePath: /data-gateway, every route is under it: /data-gateway/iot/v1/execute.

  • Every request needs the credential, except /ping, /health and /metrics (at the root and under each schema), /schemas, /version, /doc and the UI. How it is sent depends on the authentication: X-Api-Key: <key>, Authorization: Bearer <token> or Authorization: Basic <base64>.
  • ?format=beautiful indents the JSON of the answer.
  • data (the parameters of a query) and options (for example { "stage": "default" }) are JSON objects; JSON text ("data": "{\"id\": 10}") is also accepted.
  • An error answers a status and { "error", "code"?, "message" } (Errors).

docs.title: Gateway methods
State of a schema
docs.text:
Under each schema's route (/iot/v1/…), these answer only about that schema:

Method Route Answers GET /{schema}/ping 200 if the schema is ready, 503 if not GET /{schema}/health the state of the schema; 503 if it is not ready GET /{schema}/metrics the metrics of that schema GET /{schema}/version the versions of the gateway and the schema GET /{schema}/whoami the name and permissions of the credential with the authentication of that schema, and whether it has scripts enabled 
curl http://localhost:8080/iot/v1/whoami -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY"

{ "name": "reader", "permissions": ["read"], "schema": "iot/v1", "scripts": true }

The secret of the credential is never answered.

docs.title: execute
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/execute runs a query. The body is { query, data?, options? }.

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/execute?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).include(p => p.details)", "data": {"customerId": "CENTC"}}'

[
  {
    "id": 12,
    "customerId": "CENTC",
    "orderDate": "1996-07-18T00:00:00.000Z",
    "details": [
      { "orderId": 12, "productId": 21, "unitPrice": 8, "quantity": 10 },
      { "orderId": 12, "productId": 37, "unitPrice": 20.8, "quantity": 1 }
    ]
  }
]
  • A select answers the rows; update and delete answer the number of affected rows (0 when nothing matched); insert answers the inserted data.
  • With only the read permission, a query that writes (insert, update, delete, upsert, merge, bulk*) is refused with 403 before reaching the database.
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Orders.update(p => ({ freight: freight })).filter(p => p.id == id)", "data": {"id": 10248, "freight": 40}}'

1

docs.title: plan
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/plan answers how the query is executed: the dialect, the source and the sentence of each part, without running it. Body { query, options? }.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/plan -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).include(p => p.details)"}'

{
  "entity": "Orders",
  "dialect": "PostgreSQL",
  "source": "default",
  "sentence": "SELECT o.OrderID AS \"id\", o.CustomerID AS \"customerId\", o.OrderDate AS \"orderDate\", o.OrderID AS \"__id\" FROM Orders o  WHERE o.CustomerID = $1 ",
  "children": [
    {
      "entity": "Orders.details",
      "dialect": "PostgreSQL",
      "source": "default",
      "sentence": "SELECT o1.OrderID AS \"orderId\", o1.ProductID AS \"productId\", o1.UnitPrice AS \"unitPrice\", o1.Quantity AS \"quantity\", o1.OrderID AS \"LambdaOrmParentId\" FROM \"Order Details\" o1  WHERE  o1.OrderID IN ($1) "
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: model
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/model answers the shape of the result: its properties and their types.

[
  { "name": "id", "type": "integer" },
  { "name": "customerId", "type": "string" },
  { "name": "orderDate", "type": "dateTime" },
  { "name": "details", "type": "Orders.details[]", "children": [
    { "name": "orderId", "type": "integer" },
    { "name": "productId", "type": "integer" },
    { "name": "unitPrice", "type": "decimal" },
    { "name": "quantity", "type": "decimal" }
  ] }
]

docs.title: parameters
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/parameters answers the variables the query uses, which go in data.

[ { "name": "customerId", "type": "string" } ]

docs.title: constraints
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/constraints answers the constraints that apply to the entities of the query.

{ "entity": "Orders", "constraints": [], "children": [ { "entity": "Orders.details", "constraints": [] } ] }

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/metadata answers the analysed tree of the query: each sentence with its action (select, insert, …), entity, columns, parameters and constraints.

{ "classtype": "Sentence", "name": "select", "entity": "Orders", "columns": [ { "name": "id" } ], "parameters": [ { "name": "customerId", "type": "any" } ], "constraints": [] }

docs.title: script
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/script runs a script: several queries and logic in one transaction. Body { script, data?, options? }. It needs scripts.enabled (otherwise 403) and the script permission; the limits of scripts apply (maxLength, timeoutMs, maxIterations).

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "script": "order = orm.execute(\"Orders.filter(p => p.id == id)\", { id: id }); if (order.length() == 0) { throw { status: 404, message: \"order not found\" }; } order[0]",
  "data": { "id": 10248 }
}'

A script can choose the status of the answer with throw { status, message }.

docs.title: execute-queued
docs.text:
POST /{schema}/execute-queued runs a query in the background and sends its result to a Kafka topic, in chunks. It answers at once { "queueId": "…" }; the messages carry the keys <queueId>-<chunk>. Body { topic, query, data?, chunk?, options? }. It needs the queue permission (and write if the query writes) and an infrastructure.queue in the schema's lambdaORM.yaml.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute-queued -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query": "Countries.map(p => [p.iso3, p.name])", "topic": "countries", "chunk": 1000}'

The queue of a schema is configured in its lambdaORM.yaml (config is the kafkajs configuration), where consumers can also be declared:

infrastructure:
  queue:
    config: $QUEUE_CONFIG
    consumers:
      - name: syncInsights
        config: { groupId: group1 }
        subscribe: { topic: insights-sync, fromBeginning: true }
        execute: orm.execute(message.query, message.data, { stage: "insights" })

Over the WebSocket API, query.executeQueued with notify: true also tells the connection when the execution ends.

docs.title: Schema methods
docs.text:
The model of the schema. They need read. The connections of the sources are never answered.

Method Route Answers GET /{schema}/schema the version and the domain of the schema GET /{schema}/schema/version the version of the schema GET /{schema}/domain the domain: entities (properties, relations, keys, indexes, constraints) and enums GET /{schema}/entities the entities GET /{schema}/entities/{entity} one entity GET /{schema}/enums the enums GET /{schema}/enums/{enum} one enum GET /{schema}/sources the sources, with their name and dialect GET /{schema}/sources/{source} one source GET /{schema}/mappings the mappings (entities to tables and columns) GET /{schema}/mappings/{mapping} one mapping GET /{schema}/mappings/{mapping}/{entity} the mapping of one entity GET /{schema}/views the views GET /{schema}/stages the stages, with their sources GET /{schema}/stages/{stage} one stage GET /{schema}/typings the domain as TypeScript declarations (text/plain), for an editor's autocompletion 
curl http://localhost:8080/sources -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY"

[ { "name": "catalog", "dialect": "PostgreSQL" }, { "name": "accounts", "dialect": "PostgreSQL" } ]

curl http://localhost:8080/entities/Categories -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY"

{
  "name": "Categories",
  "primaryKey": ["id"],
  "uniqueKey": ["name"],
  "properties": [
    { "name": "id", "type": "integer", "required": true, "autoIncrement": true },
    { "name": "name", "type": "string", "length": 80, "required": true },
    { "name": "description", "type": "string", "length": 1000 }
  ],
  "relations": []
}

docs.title: Stage methods
docs.text:
Method Route Answers Permission GET /{schema}/stages/{stage}/exists { "exists": true } when the stage was created and its state file exists read GET /{schema}/stages/{stage}/export the rows of every entity of the stage read POST /{schema}/stages/{stage}/import imports rows (the body is an export) into the entities of the stage stageImport 
curl http://localhost:8080/stages/default/export -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" > data.json
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: $BACKEND_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Operation REST MCP tool WebSocket method Permission execute POST /execute orm_execute query.execute read (selects) / write script POST /script orm_execute_script query.script script execute queued POST /execute-queued orm_execute_queued query.executeQueued queue plan POST /plan orm_plan query.plan read metadata POST /metadata orm_metadata query.metadata read model POST /model orm_model query.model read parameters POST /parameters orm_parameters query.parameters read constraints POST /constraints orm_constraints query.constraints read schema GET /schema schema_get schema.schema read schema version GET /schema/version schema_version schema.version read domain GET /domain schema_domain schema.domain read entities GET /entities[/{entity}] schema_entities schema.entities, schema.entity read enums GET /enums[/{enum}] schema_enums schema.enums, schema.enum read sources GET /sources[/{source}] schema_sources schema.sources, schema.source read mappings GET /mappings[/{mapping}[/{entity}]] schema_mappings schema.mappings, schema.mapping, schema.entityMapping read views GET /views schema_views schema.views read stages GET /stages[/{stage}] schema_stages schema.stages, schema.stage read typings GET /typings — schema.typings read stage exists GET /stages/{stage}/exists stage_exists stage.exists read stage export GET /stages/{stage}/export stage_export stage.export read stage import POST /stages/{stage}/import stage_import stage.import stageImport version GET /version gateway_version general.version — health GET /health gateway_health general.health — ping GET /ping — general.ping —

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The authentication block has three levels: global, per transport (transports.<t>.authentication) and per schema (orm.schemas[].authentication). The most specific replaces the others (schema → transport → global). It is applied by the edge worker before anything reaches the schema.

adapter One credential (every permission) Several credentials with permissions The client sends none (default) — — nothing: an anonymous credential with every permission local, type: bearer token tokens: [{ name, value, permissions }] Authorization: Bearer <token> local, type: apikey value (and header, default X-Api-Key) keys: [{ name, value, permissions }] <header>: <key> local, type: basic username, password users: [{ username, password, permissions }] Authorization: Basic <base64(user:password)> 
authentication:
  adapter: local
  type: bearer
  tokens:
    - { name: reports, value: $REPORTS_TOKEN, permissions: [ read ] }
    - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_TOKEN, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] }
  • A local credential without its secret (or whose $VAR is not defined) stops the start. Open access is only adapter: none, written on purpose.
  • Secrets are compared in constant time. The secret never travels to the schema workers: only the name and the permissions of the credential.
  • Without a credential (or with a wrong one) the answer is 401; the WebSocket upgrades are refused.
  • /ping, /health, /metrics, /version, /schemas, /doc and the UI's files need no credential.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Allows read the schema, the domain, plan, metadata, model, parameters, constraints, stage exists and export, and execute only when every sentence is a select write execute that writes (insert, update, delete, upsert, merge, bulk*, …) script scripts (POST /script, orm_execute_script, query.script): a script can do anything inside, so it is a permission of its own queue execute-queued (and write if the query writes) stageImport importing a stage
  • Authorization happens in the schema's worker, before running anything, the same for REST, MCP and WebSocket.
  • To know whether a query writes, the gateway analyses it (its metadata): with only read, a query with any sentence that is not a select, also inside an include, is refused.
  • Without the permission: 403 in REST, status: 403 in WebSocket, isError: true in MCP, with the message the credential "reader" does not have the "write" permission.
  • GET /whoami answers the name and permissions of the credential, never its secret.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text:
Every operation that changes data, or may, leaves an audit entry: a JSON line with "type": "audit" on the standard output, so the log collector (Loki, ELK, CloudWatch, …) can keep it apart.

Operation Audited execute when some sentence is not a select script always execute queued always (when queued) stage import always 
{ "type": "audit", "time": "2026-11-17T14:03:22.114Z", "schema": "iot/v1", "transport": "mcpHttp",
  "credential": "agent", "operation": "execute", "actions": ["insert"], "entities": ["Devices"],
  "query": "Devices.insert()", "rows": 1, "durationMs": 42, "result": "ok" }
  • It is written after running, also when it fails ("result": "error" with the message).
  • It has the credential's name, never its secret. The parameters (data) are added only with audit.includeData: true, because they can have personal data. audit.enabled: false turns it off.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Limit Key When it is reached Requests per window (http only) rateLimit.windowMs, rateLimit.max (0 = off) 429 Simultaneous operations per schema server.maxConcurrent 429 with Retry-After (MCP: isError; WebSocket: status: 429) Time of an operation server.timeout error, the operation is abandoned Size of a body server.requestBodySize 413 Size of an answer server.maxResponseBytes 413: use .page(1, n) or aggregate in the query Scripts scripts.maxLength, timeoutMs, maxIterations 413 (length) or an error of the script Rows of a result for MCP mcp.maxRows cut, with a hint (MCP)

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A failed request answers a status a client can map and a JSON body:

{
  "error": "ExecutionError",
  "code": "23505",
  "message": "ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"device_types_pkey\" …"
}
Field Meaning error the name of the error: ExecutionError, ValidationError, ForbiddenError, ScriptDisabledError, … code the database's error code when there is one (Postgres SQLSTATE such as 23505, MySQL ER_DUP_ENTRY) message the message Status Cause 400 an invalid query or model (ValidationError, SchemaError, SintaxisError, LanguageError), a not null or check violation, invalid data (Postgres 22xxx) 401 no credential, or a wrong one 403 the credential lacks the permission; scripts disabled 404 a schema not exposed on that transport, an unknown route 409 a unique or foreign key violation (Postgres 23505, 23503; MySQL ER_DUP_ENTRY, ER_NO_REFERENCED_ROW_2, ER_ROW_IS_REFERENCED_2) 413 a body, an answer or a script too large 429 rate limit, or too many simultaneous operations on the schema 503 the schema is not ready (starting, in error, restarting) n a script ran throw { status: n, message } (400–599) 500 anything else

docs.title: Transports
docs.text:
The gateway has four transports. Each one listens on its own port, only when the port is configured (Configuration), and each one reaches every schema by its route.

Transport What it is Routes of the schema iot/v1 Routes of the gateway http REST API, OpenAPI 3 POST /iot/v1/execute, GET /iot/v1/entities, … /ping, /health, /metrics, /version, /schemas, /doc, /api-docs, /ui mcpHttp MCP for AI agents POST/GET/DELETE /iot/v1/mcp (Streamable HTTP); GET /iot/v1/sse + POST /iot/v1/messages?sessionId= (HTTP+SSE) GET /status mcpWebSocket MCP over WebSocket upgrade at /iot/v1/mcp GET /status, /asyncapi webSocket JSON-RPC API with notifications connection to ws://host:port/iot/v1 connection to the root: general.* and gateway.schemas; /asyncapi
  • {basePath} (transports.<t>.basePath) goes before every route: with basePath: /data-gateway, /data-gateway/iot/v1/execute and /data-gateway/ui/.
  • With a single schema at the root, its routes have no prefix (/execute, /mcp, ws://host:port/).
  • A schema that is not exposed on a transport (schemas[].transports) answers 404 there. A schema that is not ready answers 503 with the reason.
  • Each transport authenticates every request (or the WebSocket upgrade) with the effective authentication of the schema (Security).

docs.title: http
docs.text:
The REST API: every operation of λORM on a schema (queries, scripts, the schema, stages), plus the routes of the gateway. JSON in and out. Methods and examples in REST API.

transports:
  http:
    port: 8080
    basePath: /data-gateway   # optional
    swagger: { enabled: true }   # /doc and /api-docs (Swagger UI, OpenAPI 3)
    ui: { enabled: true }        # the web UI at /ui
  • GET /doc (and /api-docs) serves Swagger UI with the OpenAPI document. Its Authorize button asks for the credential as the schemas are configured: an API key in its header, a bearer token or a user and password.
  • /ping, /health and /metrics need no credential (Kubernetes probes, Prometheus).
  • The rate limit (rateLimit) applies to this transport only.

docs.title: mcpHttp
docs.text:
Model Context Protocol for AI agents: a server per schema, with a tool per operation. See MCP.

transports:
  mcpHttp:
    port: 8081
    legacySse: true    # also the older HTTP+SSE transport, for older clients
    stateful: false    # stateless: any replica answers any request, no session affinity needed
Route Protocol Clients POST/GET/DELETE {basePath}/{schema}/mcp Streamable HTTP Claude Code (--transport http), current clients GET {basePath}/{schema}/sse + POST {basePath}/{schema}/messages?sessionId=<id> HTTP+SSE (deprecated), with legacySse: true older clients GET {basePath}/status the state, the schemas and the open SSE sessions operations

The credential goes in every request (Streamable HTTP) or in the GET and every POST (SSE). HTTP+SSE keeps a session in memory: with several replicas it needs session affinity.

docs.title: mcpWebSocket
docs.text:
The same MCP servers over WebSocket. It is not a standard MCP transport: it is offered for clients and gateways that support it on their own; most clients use mcpHttp.

transports:
  mcpWebSocket:
    port: 8082
    maxConnections: 100

The connection is an upgrade at {basePath}/{schema}/mcp, authenticated in the handshake (without a credential it answers 401 and closes). The messages are JSON-RPC 2.0 with the MCP methods (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/*, …). GET {basePath}/status and GET {basePath}/asyncapi (the AsyncAPI document) are plain HTTP.

docs.title: webSocket
docs.text:
A JSON-RPC 2.0 API over one persistent connection, with the same operations as REST, plus notifications that REST cannot give: the end of a queued execution and the changes of state of the schema. See WebSocket API.

transports:
  webSocket:
    port: 8083
    maxConnections: 100
    asyncapi: { enabled: true }   # GET /asyncapi, /asyncapi.json

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
A step by step tour, from the login to a diagram, is in Getting started.

The gateway serves a web interface to explore its schemas and query them: an explorer of the schemas and their entities, the form of each entity, query tabs with the autocompletion of the domain, saved queries and diagrams of the domain. It is useful to try queries, to learn the language and to check what an agent does through MCP.

transports:
  http:
    port: 8080
    ui: { enabled: true }       # off by default

It is at http://localhost:8080/ui/ (with basePath: /data-gateway, at /data-gateway/ui/). It is served by the same http transport and calls its REST API with the credential that is entered: it has no other access.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
Home. What the Data Gateway is, its version, the schemas of the instance with their state (ready, error, …), a link to the API documentation (Swagger) and the Login button.

Login. The authentication of the instance and the credential:

Authentication Asks for API key the header (default X-Api-Key) and the key Bearer token the token Basic the user and the password None nothing

The Show / Hide button shows what was typed. The credential is checked against a schema (/whoami): a wrong one says so and stays on the page. The credential is kept only in that browser tab: closing it or reloading forgets it, and it is never stored.

Queries. The workspace, after the login: at the top, the name and permissions of the credential, the API docs and Logout (back to the home page).

At the top of every page there are two selectors:

  • Theme: System (as the operating system), Light or Dark.
  • Language: English, Español, Português, Français, Italiano, Deutsch, Nederlands, Català, Galego, Euskara.

Both are remembered by the browser.

docs.title: Explorer
docs.text:
On the left, the schemas of the instance. It can be resized by dragging its edge and hidden with the panel button of the tab bar. For each schema:

  • Domain (YAML). The domain of the schema (entities, properties, relations, keys, enums) in a read-only editor, with syntax highlighting, search and folding. It shows only the domain: never the sources, the connections nor the rest of the configuration.
  • Entities. Each entity unfolds into:
    • Properties, with their types (the primary key in bold);
    • Relations, with the related entity and the cardinality (customer → Customers · N — 1); the Open button of a relation opens the related entity. The Open button (↗) of an entity, a double click or Enter open its form.
  • What is saved in the schema: folders, queries and diagrams (below).

docs.title: Entity form
docs.text:
Like a table in a database IDE, in its own tab, with these sections:

Section Shows Properties each property: type (or enum), length, required, primary key (and unique), auto increment, default, the entity and property a foreign key references (a link to it), and its read / write expressions Relations its relations (name, type, entity, from, to, cardinality, weak) and Referenced by: the relations of other entities that point to it; each entity is a link to its form Keys and indexes primary key, unique key, indexes with their fields, constraints with their message and condition Data its rows in a table, read only, 50 per page, with Previous / Next; they can be copied and exported like any result Diagram the entity and its neighbours

The Query button opens a query tab with Entity.page(1, 10).

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
Each query is a tab, with its own schema, text, data, options and result; switching tabs loses nothing. A tab is opened with +, from an entity (Query) or from a saved query, and closed with its ×.

  • Editor with the autocompletion of the schema's domain (entities, properties, relations and functions) and the errors of λORM marked in the text while typing. Mode: query or script (scripts only when the schema has them enabled and the credential has script).
  • Data and options (JSON), and for queued executions the topic and the chunk.
  • Actions: plan, metadata, model, parameters (fills the data with the query's variables), constraints, execute (Ctrl+Enter), execute queued and, in script mode, execute script. An action the credential cannot use is disabled, and its tooltip says why.
  • Result: status, operation, time, rows and size, and four views: tree, table (when the result is a list of rows), JSON and YAML. The tree and the table show up to 200 rows; the exports have all of them.
    • The copy icon copies what is shown (the table as tab-separated text, ready to paste in a spreadsheet).
    • Export downloads the whole result as JSON, YAML or TXT (tab-separated).
  • History of the last queries of each schema, to bring one back.

docs.title: Saved queries and diagrams
docs.text:
The + of a schema or of a folder adds:

  • New folder. Folders nest, to organise what is saved.
  • New query. A query tab whose folder is that one.
  • New diagram. See Diagrams.

Each saved item has a name and a description (shown when the pointer is over it). Its row has Edit (name, description and folder) and Delete (with confirmation; a folder takes what it holds). Items are moved by dragging them onto a folder or onto the schema. Two items of the same kind cannot have the same name in a folder.

A query tab has Save (Ctrl+S) and Save as…: the first save asks for the name, the description and the folder. A • in the tab marks changes that are not saved; once saved it says saved. Opening a saved query that is already open goes to its tab.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
A diagram of the domain shows the chosen entities as boxes, with their properties, types, PK and FK (the required ones in bold), and the relations as lines with their cardinality (1 — N, 1 — 1); an inheritance is a dashed line.

New diagram asks for the name, the description, the folder and the entities: they are searched, checked one by one, or completed with Add their neighbours (the entities related to the chosen ones).

In a diagram:

Action How Lay out automatic when it opens (the boxes are placed by ELK); lay out again returns to it Move a box drag it Move a line drag it sideways; its ends stay on the rows of the fields it joins; a double click puts it back Remove an entity the × of its box (shown when the pointer is over it), or click the box and press Delete Add or remove entities Entities… Names of the relations relation names Only the names of the entities names only Zoom and move the mouse wheel; drag the background; fit shows it all Open an entity double click its box Export SVG or PNG

The diagram is saved (Save or Ctrl+S) with the place of every box and line, the names option and the entities.

docs.title: Where it is saved
docs.text:
What is saved (folders, queries, diagrams) stays in the browser, in its IndexedDB, separated by gateway and by credential: what one credential saves is not seen with another. Only the name of the credential is used for this, never its secret.

  • It is in that browser on that device: another browser or another device doesn't see it.
  • It goes if the site data of the browser is cleared. The browser is asked to keep it, and the explorer exports everything to a JSON file (⤓) and imports it back (⤒), adding to what there is or replacing it: a backup, a way to move it to another browser or to share it with someone.
  • In a browser that doesn't allow storing (some private windows), the explorer says so: what is saved lasts until the page is closed.

docs.title: In your own application
docs.text:
The UI is built with @lambdaorm/ui, a library of React components that any web application can use against a Data Gateway:

npm install @lambdaorm/ui react react-dom

import { Workspace } from '@lambdaorm/ui'
import '@lambdaorm/ui/styles.css'

<Workspace
  baseUrl="https://gateway.example.com"          // the http transport of the gateway
  headers={() => ({ 'X-Api-Key': key })}         // how to authenticate; the library keeps no credential
  locale="es"
  theme="dark"
  workspaceKey={`gateway.example.com|${user}`}   // separates what is saved
/>
Component What it is Workspace the whole workspace: explorer, entity forms, queries, saved items and diagrams QueryWorkbench one query editor with its actions and result QueryTabs several workbenches in tabs DomainDiagram a diagram of the domain (an entity and its neighbours, the whole model, or chosen entities) EntityView the form of an entity ResultViewer a result as tree, table, JSON or YAML, with copy and export

What is saved can go to another place than the browser by giving store (a WorkspaceStore, for example a backend of your own).

docs.title: WebSocket API
docs.text:
The webSocket transport offers the operations of the REST API over one persistent JSON-RPC 2.0 connection, plus notifications that REST cannot give: the end of a queued execution and the changes of state of the schema.

transports:
  webSocket:
    port: 8083

The connection is opened against the schema's route, ws://localhost:8083/iot/v1 (ws://localhost:8083/ for a single schema at the root), and is authenticated in the upgrade with the same headers as REST. A connection to the root of a gateway with several schemas has only general.* and gateway.schemas.

→ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "query.execute", "params": { "query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice)", "data": { "minPrice": 50 } } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": [ { "id": 29, "name": "Thüringer Rostbratwurst", "price": 123.79 } ] }

→ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "query.script", "params": { "script": "1 + 1" } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "error": { "code": -32000, "message": "the credential \"reader\" does not have the \"script\" permission", "data": { "name": "ForbiddenError", "status": 403 } } }

The params are the body (or the route parameters) of the equivalent REST method. An error carries in data the name and the HTTP status that REST would have answered.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Params REST equivalent general.version — GET /version general.health — GET /health general.ping — GET /ping gateway.schemas — (only at the root) GET /schemas query.execute query, data?, options? POST /execute query.script script, data?, options? POST /script query.executeQueued topic, query, data?, chunk?, options?, notify? POST /execute-queued query.plan query, options? POST /plan query.metadata query POST /metadata query.model query POST /model query.parameters query POST /parameters query.constraints query POST /constraints schema.schema — GET /schema schema.version — GET /schema/version schema.domain — GET /domain schema.entities / schema.entity — / entity GET /entities[/{entity}] schema.enums / schema.enum — / enum GET /enums[/{enum}] schema.sources / schema.source — / source GET /sources[/{source}] schema.mappings / schema.mapping / schema.entityMapping — / mapping / mapping, entity GET /mappings… schema.views — GET /views schema.stages / schema.stage — / stage GET /stages[/{stage}] schema.typings — GET /typings stage.exists stage GET /stages/{stage}/exists stage.export stage GET /stages/{stage}/export stage.import stage, data POST /stages/{stage}/import

The permissions are the same as in REST.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Messages from the server without an id:

Notification When Params queue.completed an execution queued with query.executeQueued and notify: true on this connection ended queueId, ok: true, rows (sent to the topic) queue.failed that execution failed queueId, ok: false, error schema.statusChanged the schema of the connection went to error / restarting, or back to ready path, status, reason 
→ { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 7, "method": "query.executeQueued", "params": { "topic": "countries", "query": "Countries.map(p => [p.iso3, p.name])", "chunk": 1000, "notify": true } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 7, "result": { "queueId": "q-123" } }
← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "queue.completed", "params": { "queueId": "q-123", "ok": true, "rows": 250 } }

If the schema stops being ready, the requests answer an error with status: 503; the connection stays open and works again when the schema recovers.

The AsyncAPI document of the transport is at GET /asyncapi (and /asyncapi.json). From Node, the client uses this transport with a ws:// URL.

docs.text: The labs are complete, runnable examples of λORM. Most of them are in the lambdaorm-labs repository.

docs.title: CLI labs
docs.text: Using λORM from the command line with the CLI.

docs.title: Node.js labs
docs.text: Using the @lambdaorm/lib package in a Node.js application.

docs.title: Engines lab
docs.text: The engines lab runs the same model, queries and scripts on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, Oracle and MongoDB. See Engines.
